Elena — thanks for the profile, this is very helpful. High-level recommendation up front: mix H100 for the long-context tail, A100 for steady throughput, and L4 to offload cheaper short/embedding work. Proposed initial mix (adjustable after a 2‑week pilot):

- H100 (80GB TF32 / high memory): 35% of reserved compute. Purpose: large-context summarization, models that need >64GB KV memory and higher FP throughput.
- A100 (40/80GB): 45% of reserved compute. Purpose: bulk of generative requests where batch throughput matters; good balance of memory and cost.
- L4 (48GB-ish, INT8 optimized): 20% of reserved compute. Purpose: low-cost embeddings, short-response routing, and aggressive quantized fallbacks for non-critical paths.

Rationale & tradeoffs:
- Memory: H100 gives the best headroom for 80k token windows without tiling, which reduces engineering complexity for you. A100 can handle many long requests with tiling/streaming but increases latency and engineering ops for KV stitching. L4 is memory-limited; use for <=16k token flows or after prefix cache hits.
- Latency: L4 has lower per-token latency when model fits; H100 and A100 latency depends on sequence length and batch packing. For p95 2.5s on 80k context, H100 is the least risky.
- Cost: L4 tokens are cheapest; H100 is most expensive but fewer tokens typically traverse it when we optimize routing and cache.
- Operational: suggest reserved baseline with burst pool (dedicated reserved + burst on-hosted) for ~25% extra capacity during reports. Also propose aggressive KV prefix caching for the frequent clinical templates to cut effective token usage.

Next steps: I'll loop in Dev for kernel/tiling notes and a simple proposal PDF that you can attach to procurement. Can we book a 45m sizing call Thurs 5/28?

Jordan / team — adding some technical detail you can include in the proposal. Quoted below for context.

On 2026-05-27, Jordan wrote: 
> Proposed initial mix (adjustable after a 2‑week pilot): H100 35% / A100 45% / L4 20%

Notes for procurement & ops:
- Workload mapping: route by request shape not by endpoint. Use quick pre-routing classifier: if request has >30k tokens OR requires full-document attention, route to H100; else if batchable and latency tolerant, route to A100; short/embedding -> L4. This keeps H100 usage focused and predictable.
- Memory/tiling: for 80k windows we recommend a hybrid approach — sticky H100 sessions with KV eviction + chunked attention for A100 when cost-constrained. Tiling on A100 increases CPU-side stitching; budget ~5-10ms extra latency per chunk.
- Quantization & fallbacks: L4 runs INT8/4-bit quantized variants for embeddings and short responses. For customer-facing high-quality summaries keep non-quantized on H100/A100 until we validate quality using your eval set.
- Autoscale & hedging: reserve 60-70% for steady traffic, keep 30-40% as burst capacity (shared across regions). Enable fast cold-starts with warm replicas for H100 (spin-up targets <60s).
- Ops tolerance: propose initial commit for 12 months with quarterly re-eval. Add a 2-week paid pilot at 50% of the expected reserved commit to validate traffic shape and cache hit rates; we’ll re-tune mix after pilot.

Sizing heuristics (very rough starting numbers you can use in procurement doc):
- Long-context summarization (80k): ~1.8–2.5 tokens/sec per H100 slot (depending on model & batch packing).
- A100 throughput: ~3–5 tokens/sec per slot for mid-sized models with good batching.
- L4: ~6–12 tokens/sec for short requests/embeddings (quantized).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: underestimating peak concurrency -> mitigation: burst pool + circuit-breaker routing.
- Risk: cache miss storms for new reports -> mitigation: pre-warm prefixes, gradual rollout.
